entities.summary:
Agencia EFE, established in 1939, is Spain's leading news agency, headquartered in the Edificio Génesis in Madrid. This institution emerged during a tumultuous period in Spanish history marked by the Spanish Civil War, which began in the same year it was founded. The agency's role in disseminating news across Spain and internationally has made it an essential player in the propagation of information in the Spanish-speaking world, influencing public opinion and political discourse for decades.

From its inception, EFE has expanded its reach significantly, becoming a vital source of news covering various topics including politics, economics, and culture. It began with a few employees and has grown to employ thousands of journalists globally, establishing more than 180 offices worldwide by the early 21st century. The agency has been pivotal in reporting on major historical events, such as Spain's transition to democracy in the late 1970s and its integration into the European Union in 1986, providing a consistent narrative that shaped public understanding of these critical transitions.

The legacy of Agencia EFE extends beyond just news reporting; it has set standards for journalism in Spain and Latin America, influencing the development of other news agencies. As a member of the European Alliance of News Agencies, EFE has contributed to the professionalization of news dissemination, promoting ethical standards and journalistic integrity. Its archives serve as a historical record, capturing the evolution of Spanish society and politics over the past century.

A striking testament to EFE's influence is its role in the coverage of the 2004 Madrid train bombings, where its reporting was among the first to provide accurate information in real-time. In the words of EFE's former director, 'We are not just chroniclers of events; we are the guardians of history.'
